methods.label: Use the parity of each pair
methods.explanation:
Separate the six integers into the three pairs added at each stage. Their sums are
\[
26,\qquad 41-26=15,\qquad 57-41=16.
\]
Two even integers have an even sum, and two odd integers also have an even sum. Thus the middle pair, whose sum is odd, must contain one even integer and one odd integer. Every allowed list therefore has at least one even integer.

To see that one is enough, take the integers in order to be
\[
13,\ 13,\ 7,\ 8,\ 7,\ 9.
\]
Their successive totals are \(26\), \(41\), and \(57\), and only \(8\) is even. Hence the minimum is \(\boxed{1}\), choice A.
